entries.name: Age
entries: Shades appear as the age they were when they died. They potentially have no limit to their lifespan, but, realistically, ancient shades grow weary and lose their hold on their memories, fading away near 750 years old.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Shades come from all walks of life but tend toward neutrality. Shades that lack contact with other people grow more selfish over time and slip toward evil.

entries.name: Size
entries: Your size is determined by your Living Origin.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your speed is determined by your Living Origin.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: Your existence beyond death makes you at home in the dark. You can see in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} within 60 feet of you as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} and in darkness as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Ghostly Flesh
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your action to dissolve your physical body into the ephemeral stuff of spirits. You become translucent and devoid of color, and the air around you grows cold. Your transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you end it as a bonus action. During it, you have a flying speed of 30 feet with the ability to hover, and you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't made with silvered weapons. In addition, you have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape a grapple or against being {@condition restrained}, and you can move through creatures and solid objects as if they were {@quickref difficult terrain||3}. If you end your turn inside an object, you take {@damage 1d10} force damage. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Imperfect Undeath
entries: You are a humanoid, but your partial transition into undeath makes you susceptible to effects that target undead. Though you can regain hit points from spells like cure wounds, you can also be affected by game effects that specifically target undead, such as a cleric's Turn Undead feature. Game effects that raise a creature from the dead work on you as normal, but they return you to life as a shade. A true resurrection or wish spell can restore you to life as a fully living member of your original race.

entries.name: Life Drain
entries: When you damage a creature with an attack or a spell, you can choose to deal extra necrotic damage to the target equal to your level. If the creature's race matches your Living Origin, you gain temporary hit points equal to the necrotic damage dealt. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Spectral Resilience
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against poison and disease, and you have resistance to necrotic damage.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language spoken by your Living Origin.

entries.name: Living Origin
entries: As living echoes of who they once were, shades maintain some of the traits they bore in life. Choose another race as your Living Origin. This is the race you were in life. Your size and speed are those of your Living Origin, and you know one language spoken by your Living Origin.

entries.name: Shadow Goblin Traits
entries: You are a shadow goblin, forever changed by the Shadow Realm, setting you apart from other goblins.

entries.name: Age
entries: Shadow goblins reach adulthood at age 8 and can live up to 70 years.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Much like the shadow fey they coexist with, shadow goblins are not inherently evil, despite their reputations. Their natures are a constant balance between whimsy and being useful and productive. Shadow goblins are more likely to tend toward neutral good or neutral alignments.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You can see in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} within 60 feet as though it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} and in darkness as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Quick Wit
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Deception} and {@skill Insight} skills.

entries.name: Shadow Camoflauge
entries: You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made to hide in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} or darkness.

entries.name: Stink Eye
entries: As an action, you can perform a combination of rude gestures and sounds to distract one creature you can see within 30 feet. If the target can hear and see you, it must make a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your Charisma ability modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failure, it has disadvantage on the next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

entries.name: Unseelie Blessing
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed}, and magic can't put you to sleep.

entries.name: Language
entries: You can speak, read, and write Goblin and Umbral.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your walking speed is 30 feet, and you have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

entries.name: Bejeweled Carapace
entries: When you are hit with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Silken Legacy
entries: You know the {@spell Thaumaturgy} cantrip. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell Find Familiar} spell (the familiar takes the form of a jeweled insect or arachnid) using this trait, and starting at 5th level, you can cast the {@spell Web}  spell using this trait, both without material components. Once you cast {@spell Find Familiar} or Web  with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).

entries.name: Chilled Anatomy
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage. You also know the {@spell Ray of Frost|XPHB} cantrip.

entries.name: Compacted Snow
entries: You can move through the space of any creature that is a size larger than you, but you can't stop in the same space. Additionally, you can squeeze through a space that is large enough for a creature one size smaller than you without movement penalties.

entries.name: Frigid Construct
entries: You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in 4 hours if you spend those hours unmoving; during this time you are indistinguishable from a snowman, but retain consciousness. You don't need to eat, drink or breathe.

entries.name: Glacial Form
entries: Once per long rest, you can cast the {@spell False Life|XPHB} spell without using the material components or expending a spell slot, and harden your body into ice.

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: You are a Construct.

entries.name: Size
entries: You are Medium or Small. You choose the size when you select this species.

entries.name: Argent Gleam
entries: As a bonus action, you can channel a mote of the Silver Path's light with your choice of one of the following options:
Path's grace. You cast the {@spell Bless} spell, requiring no material components.
Zealous charge. You take the {@action Dash} action. The first time you make an attack roll before the end of your turn, on a hit or miss, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d6} radiant damage.
Once you use this trait's bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Silver Bulwark
entries: You can call upon the Silver Path to protect you. When you take bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, you can use your reaction to gain resistance to those three damage types until the start of your next turn. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Age
entries: Strigs reach maturity faster than most birdfolk races, around 15 years. They can reach a respectable old age by birdfolk standards, living around 80 years.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Strigs are normally good aligned, having a strong sense of fair play as well as a tendency to see the best in others. They also favor chaotic alignments, as strigs are a freedom-loving people who will usually put their personal morals above any imposed system of governance.

entries.name: Size
entries: Strigs are muscular, imposing folk ranging from 4 to over 5 feet tall and weighing around 110 pounds. Your size is Medium.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

entries.name: Glide
entries: Using your feathered arms, you can slow your fall, and glide short distances. When falling you can use your reaction to spread your arms, stiffen your wing feathers, and slow your descent. While doing so, you continue to fall gently at a speed of 60 feet per round, taking no fall damage when you land. If you would fall at least 10 feet in this way, you may fly up to your movement speed in one direction you choose, although you cannot choose to move upwards, landing in the space you finish your movement. You cannot glide while carrying heavy weapons or wielding a shield (though you may drop any held items as part of your reaction to spread your arms). You cannot glide while wearing heavy armor, or if you are encumbered.

entries.name: Talons
entries: Your sharp claws aid you in unarmed combat and while climbing. Your damage for an unarmed strike is {@damage 1d4} piercing damage. Additionally, you have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks made to climb any surface your talons could reasonably grip.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You are adept at hunting under the cover of night. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Patterned Feathers
entries: You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks when you attempt to hide in a forest.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Birdfolk. You can also understand Auran, though you cannot speak it naturally.

entries.name: Guiding Light
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can produce dim light in a 20 ft radius from your nose. You can end this effect as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Antler Defence
entries: Once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can lower your antlers and enter a defensive stance. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +2 bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} against melee attacks.

entries.name: Hooves
entries: If you hit a target with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d4} plus your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Born to Navigate
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill.

name: The Disembodied
entries: You possess certain traits as a result of the magical mishap that trapped you between worlds. The disembodied are a collection of species that were in Ulmur's Gate when the accident occurred. Because of this, you can choose what species you appear as. This also affects some features below, such as your height. Unless specified, you do not gain any features from your origin species.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Intelligence score increases by 2 and your Dexterity score increases by 1.

entries.name: Age
entries: The disembodied mature at a much slower rate than their humanoid equivalent, and their life expectancy is drastically higher, with not a single disembodied having passed due to old age.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: The disembodied tend towards no particular alignments.

entries.name: Size
entries: You still possess the height of your former humanoid self, but your nearly insubstantial nature has drastically reduced your weight to a quarter of your original weight. Your size is the same it was before the accident.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

entries.name: Fade Away
entries: On your turn, as an action, you can fade from the Material Realm and disappear into the ethereal plane. While you remain faded away, you cannot interact with the Material Plane, and effects on the Material Plane cannot interact with you, including spells and creatures. However, you can move and hear as normal, and see everything in shades of grey.

This effect lasts for 1 minute, or until you use a bonus action to end it. When the effect ends, you reappear on the Material Plane, in the closest unoccupied space you disappeared from. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

entries.name: Planar Outcast
entries: You may cast the {@spell feather fall} spell once per day, targeting yourself only. When you reach 3rd level, you may cast the {@spell blur} spell once per day. When you reach 5th level, you may cast the {@spell blink} spell once per day. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

entries.name: Natural Weapon
entries: You have fangs, hooves, or claws, which serve as a natural weapon. Work with your GM to determine what type of natural weapon you possess and decide whether it deals Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage. You can use your natural weapon to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you hit with it, you deal {@damage 1d6} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier damage (choose which during character creation) of your chosen type, instead of the Bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed attack.

entries.name: Trollish Regeneration
entries: The regenerative power in your blood allows you to quickly recover from wounds. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend any number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} up to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If you take Acid or Fire damage, you lose access to this ability until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Natural Adaptation
entries: You manifest different traits depending on your non-humanoid ancestor. Choose one of the ancestor types from the Trollkin Ancestry table. You gain a different benefit depending on your choice.

entries.caption: Trollkin Ancestry
rows: When you make an ability check that uses Charisma, you may roll a {@dice 1d6} and add it to the total. You can use this trait a number of times per day equal to your Charisma modifier, and you regain all uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saves to avoid or escape grapples. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

entries.name: Age
entries: Your natural aging process slows and becomes similar to that of an elf or shadow fey.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Umbral humans have often walked a troubling path to become what they are. This tends to push umbral humans toward neutral or chaotic alignments, but all variations exist.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You can see in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} within 60 feet as though it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} and in darkness as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Dark Infusion
entries: You have resistance to cold damage.

entries.name: Fade Away
entries: While standing perfectly still, you can use an action to become {@condition invisible}. You become visible again if you move or take an action. You can use this feature a number of times per day equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Language
entries: You can speak, read, and write Common and Umbral.

entries.name: Age
entries: Vulpins mature at an average pace, and can be comparatively long-lived. They reach adulthood at 15 years, and live well past 90 years.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Vulpins aren't innately evil, but their difficulty empathizing with others means they are only rarely good aligned. Most vulpins find strict authority distasteful, preferring chaotic alignments over lawful ones.

entries.name: Size
entries: Vulpins cut dashing figures and are usually lean and muscular. They stand between 4 and a half and 5 and a half feet tall, but are relatively lightweight, weighing between 90 and 140 pounds. Your size is Medium.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You are adept at hunting at night. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Bite
entries: You have sharp fangs that enable you to make natural bite attacks. You can choose to bite as an unarmed strike that deals {@damage 1d6} points of piercing damage, which can be calculated using either your Strength or Dexterity modifier for both the attack roll and damage bonus.

entries.name: Evasive
entries: You add your Intelligence modifier as a bonus on all Dexterity saving throws.

entries.name: Bewitching Guile
entries: You can cast {@spell charm person} as a 1st level spell with this trait, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast {@spell ambush prey|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} as a 2nd level spell with this trait, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. When you reach 5th level, you can cast {@spell fear} with this trait, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Birdfolk and Vulpin.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Small (Wechselkind are between 2 and 3 feet tall and weigh between 35 and 55 pounds.)

speedEntry.name: Speed:
entries: 30 feet. You can reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 5 feet to gain an extra traditional trait.

items.name: Age:
entries: Wechselkind do not age as normal creatures do, forever trapped in the doll-like visage of their creation. Their maximum age is a function of natural wear and damage, and they are immune to magical aging effects.

entries.name: Traditional Wechselkind Traits
entries: The magical and artificial nature shapes the aptitudes and innate features of all Wechselkind.

entries.name: Trait Selection
entries: Selecting the traditional traits noted for your heritage is quick and easy, and creates a character who feels like a solid archetype within your chosen heritage. But you can swap any of those suggested traditional heritage traits for {@filter any of the traits provided|optionalfeatures|source=GrimHollowPG24|feature type=HT}, building your character around any eight traits. This can include taking the traditional traits presented for any other heritage, taking one of your traditional traits again to gain its secondary effect, or taking any of the many traits that aren't part of any heritage's default presentation.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Constitution score increases by 2 and your Charisma score increases by 1.

entries.name: Age
entries: As constructs, the wechselkind do not age as normal creatures do. They are forever trapped in the doll-like body of a stolen child. As such, their maximum age is more a function of natural erosion and damage than of time, occasionally needing to replace or fix body parts when needed. You are immune to magical aging effects.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Faerie are as close to the embodiment of chaos as most mortals are likely to see, and their creations usually follow that trend. Although some tend towards mischief, more wechselkind lean towards good than evil.

entries.name: Size
entries: Built to resemble a child, wechselkind are between 2 and 3 feet tall and weigh between 35 and 55 pounds. Your size is Small.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

entries.name: Artificial Form
entries: As a constructed creature, your body functions differently than a normal person. You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition poisoned}, and you have resistance to poison damage. You are immune to disease. You don't need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe. You are still considered humanoid.

entries.name: Faerie Glamour
entries: When the faerie leaves a wechselkind in place of a mortal child, they cover it with a glamour to make it appear identical to the child that was stolen. Over time this glamour fades, but a wechselkind can still call upon it in times of need. You may cast the {@spell disguise self} spell once with this trait, but only to take on the appearance of the child you were intended to replace, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

entries.name: Childish Agility
entries: You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Acrobatics} skill.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write Sylvan and one other language of your choice.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 5-6 feet tall)

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Claws
entries: You have wickedly sharp claws that you can use to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you hit with your claws, you deal {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier Slashing damage, instead of the Bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

entries.name: Predatory Prowess
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Perception|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill (your choice).

entries.name: Scent
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks relating to detecting scents and tracking.

entries.name: Shift Aspect
entries: You can transform as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, gaining the primal power of your lycanthropic forebears. The transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you end it (no action required). Once you transform, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
When you transform, you gain one of the following options (choose the option each time you transform).

items.name: Bestial Strength
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks as well as any checks or saves to resist or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Primal Savagery
entries: You channel the raw savagery of your bestial side. When you use this option, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your turns while it is active, you can roar. Creatures other than your allies within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your Charisma modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. A creature that succeeds on the save has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to your roar for 24 hours.

items.name: Swift Hunter
entries: Your body becomes primed for the hunt. Until the transformation ends, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is increased by 10 feet, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4–5 feet tall)

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Keen Senses
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception|XPHB} skill, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

entries.name: Bite
entries: Your formidable jaws are a natural weapon, which you can use to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. If you hit with them, you deal Piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Strength modifier in place of the normal Bludgeoning damage of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: For the Pack
entries: You can use the {@action Help|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: Your dense fur and thick hide provide you with natural armor. While you aren't wearing armor, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equals 13 plus your Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Quadruped
entries: You have several traits based on your quadrupedal body shape.

items.name: Hands Off
entries: You cannot hold items in your paws, and you cannot wield weapons or a {@item Shield|XPHB} unless otherwise noted in the weapon's description (see {@item Steel Jaws|FoEQuickstone}). You can perform the Somatic components of spells with your front paws but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks that require fine manipulation.

items.name: Sturdy Steed
entries: You can carry a rider of Medium size or smaller. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

items.name: Battle Beast
entries: You cannot wear armor designed for Humanoids, you must wear barding instead. The cost is four times the equivalent armor made for Humanoids, and it weighs twice as much.

items.name: Vertically Challenged
entries: Any climb that requires hands is especially difficult for you. When you make such a climb, each foot of movement costs you 4 extra feet, instead of the normal 1 extra foot.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Small or Medium (Wulven are the same general height as others of their original heritage, but are often stockier, more muscular, or lither depending on the nature of the curse.)

speedEntry.name: Speed:
entries: 30 feet. If you are Small, you can reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 5 feet to gain an extra traditional trait.

items.name: Age:
entries: Wulven mature at the same rate as others of their original heritage, but the magic that spawns them lessens the debilitating effects of aging, and they remain fit even in their later years.

entries.name: Traditional Wulven Traits
entries: Many Wulven channel the natural instincts—and often the natural fierceness—of the creature their curse links them to.

entries.name: Trait Selection
entries: Selecting the traditional traits noted for your heritage is quick and easy, and creates a character who feels like a solid archetype within your chosen heritage. But you can swap any of those suggested traditional heritage traits for {@filter any of the traits provided|optionalfeatures|source=GrimHollowPG24|feature type=HT}, building your character around any eight traits. This can include taking the traditional traits presented for any other heritage, taking one of your traditional traits again to gain its secondary effect, or taking any of the many traits that aren't part of any heritage's default presentation.
